threads.body: [General] This literal-matching guarantee is not honored. Both deprecated methods still delegate to `DefaultHttpServerInstrumenterBuilder#setCaptured*Headers`, which builds an `IncludeExclude`; `CapturedHttpHeaders` then treats `*` and `?` as wildcards now that this module enumerates names. An existing `"*"` value will therefore capture every request/response header, including credentials, contrary to the documented compatibility requirement. Route the deprecated methods through an exact-name representation before enabling enumeration.

@@ -52,22 +53,68 @@ public SpringWebMvcTelemetryBuilder addAttributesExtractor( return this; } + /** + * Configures which HTTP request headers are captured as span attributes. + * + *

Selector patterns are matched case-insensitively, since HTTP header names are + * case-insensitive. {@code ?} matches one character and {@code *} matches any number of + * characters, including none. Excluded patterns take precedence over included patterns. A + * selector with no included patterns captures every header that is not excluded, while an + * {@linkplain IncludeExclude#isEmpty() empty} selector, like no selector at all, captures no + * headers. + */ + @CanIgnoreReturnValue + public SpringWebMvcTelemetryBuilder setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude requestHeaders) { + builder.setRequestHeaders(requestHeaders); + return this; + } + /** * Configures HTTP request headers to capture as span attributes. * + *

The header names are matched literally. Unlike {@link #setRequestHeaders(IncludeExclude)}, + * {@code *} and {@code ?} are not treated as glob patterns, since this setting never documented + * them as wildcards.

replies.body:
This is accurate against this branch's head in isolation, but not against what ships. The base branch `trask/http-header-selectors-api` gained commit `1572a0077b` ("Match deprecated captured header names literally") after this branch last diverged from it. That commit changes `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` / `setCapturedResponseHeaders` to call `httpAttributesExtractorBuilder.setCaptured*Headers` directly, which routes through the new `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact` and stores the names in a literal `exactOnlyNames` set instead of building an `IncludeExclude`. So delegating here is exactly the "exact-name representation" you're asking for.

I deliberately did not rebase to pick that commit up, because CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge` and a force-push would clear the review check run.

I did verify the merged behavior rather than assume it: I merged `origin/trask/http-header-selectors-api` into a scratch branch and ran the module tests there. The new `deprecatedSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally` test in this PR passes a legacy value of `"*"` through the deprecated setters and asserts that no `http.request.header.*` or `http.response.header.*` attribute is emitted. It fails on this branch's head alone — precisely the bug you describe — and passes on the merged state.

Follow-up with harder evidence than my previous reply, which cited a locally reconstructed merge. I have now run this against the actual commit CI builds, `refs/pull/19607/merge` = `fd0c37f22e` ("Merge 9cb07b6897 into 1572a0077b"), which does contain the base-branch fix.

All 15 tests across the five new `*HeaderCaptureTest` classes pass there, including `deprecatedSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally` in each module. That test pushes a legacy value of `"*"` through `setCapturedRequestHeaders` / `setCapturedResponseHeaders` and asserts no `http.request.header.*` or `http.response.header.*` attribute is emitted.

The contrast is the point: the same test run against this PR's head commit in isolation fails in all five modules, with `http.request.header.x-test-request`, `http.request.header.x-secret-token`, `http.response.header.x-test-response` and `http.response.header.x-secret-token` all present on the span — exactly the credential-widening you describe. So the finding is accurate about the head branch alone and does not survive the merge.

The test is part of this PR precisely so this stays evidence rather than an argument, and so it fails loudly if the globbing path is ever reintroduced.

replies.body: Same as the equivalent thread on the webmvc-6.0 builder: the base branch commit `1572a0077b` makes `DefaultHttpServerInstrumenterBuilder#setCaptured*Headers` store the names literally via `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact`, so this delegation is the exact-name path. Verified by merging the current base into a scratch branch and running the module tests, where the new `deprecatedSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally` test confirms a legacy `"*"` captures no headers.
